Plot an INLAvanilla fit

Source: R/methods.R
plot.inla_vanilla.Rd

By default (type = "marg_pdf"), draws the marginal density of each parameter, on the unconstrained scale, with the Gaussian marginal of the Laplace approximation for comparison. The vertical line marks the posterior mean. For a fit with marginals = "gaussian" the marginals are Gaussian: centred at the VB mean, or, with vb = FALSE, the Laplace marginals themselves, drawn without a second copy.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'inla_vanilla'
plot(
  x,
  pars = NULL,
  type = c("marg_pdf", "sn_fit", "sn_fit_log"),
  laplace = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class inla_vanilla.

pars

Parameters to plot, by name or position. Defaults to all.

type

The plot: "marg_pdf" (the default) for the marginal densities, "sn_fit" for each skew-normal fit against its scan, or "sn_fit_log" for the same on a log scale, as INLAvaan names them.

laplace

Logical. Overlay the Laplace (Gaussian) marginals? Default TRUE; ignored when the marginals are the Laplace ones, and by the "sn_fit" plots.

...

Further graphical parameters passed to graphics::plot() for each panel, such as xlab or main; they replace the defaults (the parameter name as the title, no axis labels, and for "marg_pdf" no y axis).

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

type = "sn_fit" shows each skew-normal fit against the scan it was fitted to, as INLAvaan's plot(type = "sn_fit") does. The x axis is the scan coordinate, in posterior SDs from the mode (the Laplace SDs, from -4 to 4). "Raw" is the log-posterior along the scan and "Corrected" the same with the volume correction gamma1 added, each as a density scaled to a peak of 1, and "Skew-normal fit" is the fitted skew-normal at the height it was fitted at. The largest gap between the last two, as a fraction of the peak, is the NMAD of summary.inla_vanilla(). type = "sn_fit_log" draws the same on a base-10 log scale, which shows the tails. Both use the scans kept in the fit, with no further calls of logpost, and need skew-normal marginals.
